extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians and comedy writers crafting an hour-long special
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for structuring, editing, and performing a stand-up comedy hour so it coheres around a single idea, balances joke and story density, and manages a comedic-to-devastating emotional arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single articulable thesis
rubrics_metrics.description: The strongest hours have ONE thesis (Jigsaw: a partner is not a puzzle piece for completion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hour should be organized around a single, expressible idea that everything relates back to. Use that thesis to give the hour meaning and cohesion; name or be able to state the thesis succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every bit serves the thesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Every joke either supports the thesis, complicates it, or earns the right to land harder by association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each joke by whether it ties to the thesis in one of these ways. Bits that do not relate to the thesis should be considered for removal, regardless of how well they perform in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to cut killer jokes that don't fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Are you willing to cut killer jokes that don't fit?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to remove 'killer' material if it doesn't serve the thesis or arc. The talk explicitly states: 'Jokes that don't relate are cut, even if they kill in isolation.' Prioritize overall cohesion over isolated laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke-density arc: highest at the beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Is joke density highest at the beginning? Open with high JOKE density — establish you can be funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the hour so the front-load demonstrates comedic capability (high premise/joke density), mid-hour transitions into longer stories (slower joke density), and late-hour reduces joke density to allow sincerity. This arc builds audience patience and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned right to devastate (funny-to-devastating pivot)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the audience earned the right to be devastated by the end? Train the audience to laugh at a register they trust (light, recognizable). Use that trust to pivot, late in the hour, into something painful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build emotional capital by consistently delivering laughs in a familiar register; those laughs become the currency for a late, painful pivot. The audience must be prepared and emotionally invested for a devastating turn to land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience emotional contract — deliver early and abundantly
rubrics_metrics.description: They came to laugh; you must deliver early and abundantly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you fail to fulfill this expectation early, the audience will not follow you later. Once you deliver the expected laughs, the audience is more willing to go with you into riskier or more serious territory. Betraying that contract early loses them permanently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Callbacks should be discovered, not engineered
rubrics_metrics.description: Are callbacks discovered, not engineered? The audience must feel they DISCOVERED the callback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant subtle seeds rather than overtly setting up callbacks. A callback works because of earlier investment; avoid drawing attention to the setup so the audience experiences recognition and discovery, which increases payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tags should hit the same target from a different angle
rubrics_metrics.description: A tag should hit the same target with a different angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tagging, find new perspectives on the same target rather than repeating the same joke. Tags should deepen or vary the joke's attack, leveraging audience familiarity without redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Callback seeding vs. setup anti-pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Never set up the callback, just place the seed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid explicit setups that telegraph future callbacks. Instead, casually introduce elements early so the later callback feels earned and discovered. The anti-pattern is engineering obvious, heavy-handed setups that reduce payoff.
